Connor Zilisch says every trip through the Phoenix dogleg registers about a 10G hit on his mouthpiece sensor. He is torn on whether NASCAR should change it. The dogleg is a bend on the Phoenix frontstretch, near the start/finish line. Drivers can cut low across the flat area below it, which used to be grass, before climbing back onto the banked racing surface. The data came from a mouthpiece sensor that many Cup drivers wear.
